text:
Not all low mood is depression. Demoralization describes a loss of confidence in one's ability to cope. Its hallmark is subjective incompetence: the person is willing to act but unsure how to move forward. Pleasure helps tell the two apart. In demoralization, the capacity for pleasure is usually still present. In a depressive episode, it usually fades. The two can occur separately or together, so the distinction is a prompt to look closer, never a reason to overlook depression. Demoralization is listed in ICD-11 under code MB22.2, and it is not in DSM-5-TR.

Where the evidence stops:
• Most demoralization research comes from cancer and palliative care, so its separation from depression in physically well adults is not yet established.

Key source: de Figueiredo, 2026, The Journal of Clinical Psychiatry: https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.26com16383
